newsitem.title: UK: Britain backs U.S. call for global ban on mines. [CORRECTED 09:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Britain backs U.S. call for global ban on mines. [CORRECTED 09:05 GMT]

text.p: Britain on Saturday welcomed the United States' announcement that it will seek a worldwide ban on landmines at a disarmament conference due to begin in Geneva on Monday.
"We welcome the announcement by the U.S...The U.S. proposal is closely in line with UK policy. We fully support it," Britain's foreign ministry said in a statement.

President Clinton's spokesman said on Friday that Washington. would unilaterally observe a permanent ban on the export of anti-personnel mines and seek to initiate negotiations for a global ban at the United Nations conference.
The ban is aimed at mines designed to injure people rather than anti-tank mines, larger weapons designed to immobilise armoured vehicles.
Britain ran into a row over its policy on mines last week, after Princess Diana called for an international ban on the "hideous weapons" when she visited Angola and met casualties of its 20-year war.
She outraged some ruling Conservatives who saw her words as an endorsement of the opposition Labour Party's policy.
The government backs a ban on most anti-personnel mines, but says this should exclude so-called "smart mines", which self-destruct after a period of time.
Britain exports military equipment worth around five billion pounds ($8.4 billion) each year, but it has agreed to destroy its stockpiles of anti-personnel mines if a ban is agreed.
(Corrects to remove erroneous reference to Britain being one of the biggest mine manufacturers.)
